member.name: T:Sitecore.Collections.LockSet
member.summary:
A collection of low-grained objects provided based on callee .
As equal must have same hash codes, returns same lock for equal .
The lock granularity (number of internal locks) is controlled by .
The higher nubmer of locks, the lower chances different objects will be routed to same object lock. Not equal objects might produce same hash codes, thereby certain collisions might occur.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.KnownSettings.BulkUpdateContextSettings.DescendantsRebuildThreshold
member.summary:
Gets the descendants rebuild threshold.
Under active BulkUpdateContext, table Descendants is not updated, but all operations are enqueued to be performed when leaving the BulkUpdateContext. The setting is used to check if number of the operations exceeds the value of the setting, then full descendants rebuild is performed; otherwise, the enqueued operations are executed. Default value: 1000. In order to change the setting's value, add setting "BulkUpdateContext.DescendantsRebuildThreshold" with your custom value into configuration.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.KnownSettings.CachingSettings.CacheKeyIndexing.PathCacheEnabled
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the system uses extended indexed storage for cache keys of the PathCache.
member.remarks: Using indexed storage for PathCache keys insignificantly slows adding item paths to the PathCache. However, it can drastically reduce the time it takes to perform partial cache clearing of the PathCache. This setting is useful on large solutions where items are frequently renamed, moved, copied and deleted.
member.value: true if the system uses extended indexed storage for cache keys of the PathCache; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.KnownSettings.CachingSettings.CacheKeyIndexing.DefaultInnerContainerCapacity
member.summary: Gets the default inner container capacity for caches.
member.remarks: The value of the setting is used for creating inner containers in some caches to optimize memory consumption. Increasing the value increases memory consumption. It may be needed to improve performance if you process many versions and languages of the same item. Default value: 4. In order to change the value, add setting Cache.CacheKeyIndexingEnabled.DefaultInnerContainerCapacity into Sitecore.config, <settings> section.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.KnownSettings.CoreSettings.AliasesActive
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether aliases are active.
member.value: True, if aliases are active, otherwise false. Default value: true.

remarks.para: When Sitecore renders a page, it first tries to determine the current item from the path on the query string. If the path does not match an item, it search the alias list for matching pages. An alias is a simple pointer to an item in Sitecore. If a match is found, that page is rendered.
Aliases are configured in /sitecore/system/aliases.
Aliases cause a small performance loss as the alias list has to be searched, if the page was not found.
This setting controls if the alias list search or not.
The name of the web.config setting is "AliasesActive".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.KnownSettings.CoreSettings.AllowLogoutOfAllUsers
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the logout screen presents all users or just users with the same name.
member.value: True, if all users are shown, otherwise false. Default value: false.

remarks.para: >When a user logs in, Sitecore checks if the maximum number of users has been reached (as specified in the license). If so, the logout user web page is shown allowing the user to logout a existing session.

This flags is the user is allowed to logout only sessions with the same name as the user, or all other sessions. For instance if the flag is false, the user "Andy" may only logout other sessions created by the user "Andy". If the flag is true, "Andy" can also logout sessions created by "Bob".
The name of the web.config setting is "AllowLogoutOfAllUsers".

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the struct.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.KnownSettings.LanguageFallbackSettings.AllowVaryFallbackSettingsPerLanguage
member.summary:
If set to 'true', then values from both versioned 'Enable Language Fallback' and shared 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox fields on the field definition item are used to determine whether language fallback functionality should be enabled for the corresponding field. It allows you to have different fallback settings for the same field in different content languages.
Example: when 'en-CA' tries to fallback to 'en', the checkbox field will be retrieved from the field definition item in 'en-CA', thus such version should exist. If retrieved value is 'false', then the 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox field is used.
Note: enabling this feature has negative impact on performance.
If set to 'false', only the shared 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox field on the field definition item is used to determine whether language fallback functionality should be enabled for the corresponding field.
Default value: false.
member.value: true if allow vary fallback settings per language; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.AliasesActive
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether aliases are active.
member.value: True, if aliases are active, otherwise false. Default value: true.

remarks.para: When Sitecore renders a page, it first tries to determine the current item from the path on the query string. If the path does not match an item, it search the alias list for matching pages. An alias is a simple pointer to an item in Sitecore. If a match is found, that page is rendered.
Aliases are configured in /sitecore/system/aliases.
Aliases cause a small performance loss as the alias list has to be searched, if the page was not found.
This setting controls if the alias list search or not.
The name of the web.config setting is "AliasesActive".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.AllowLogoutOfAllUsers
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the logout screen presents all users or just users with the same name.
member.value: True, if all users are shown, otherwise false. Default value: false.

remarks.para: >When a user logs in, Sitecore checks if the maximum number of users has been reached (as specified in the license). If so, the logout user web page is shown allowing the user to logout a existing session.

This flags is the user is allowed to logout only sessions with the same name as the user, or all other sessions. For instance if the flag is false, the user "Andy" may only logout other sessions created by the user "Andy". If the flag is true, "Andy" can also logout sessions created by "Bob".
The name of the web.config setting is "AllowLogoutOfAllUsers".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.AppendQSToUrlRendering
member.summary: Gets a value indicating whether main query strings are appended to URL renderings?
member.remarks: If true, query strings of the main page will be passed on the all URL renderings on the page.
member.example: If a layout contains a URL rendering with the URL http://www.google.com/search., and the layout is triggered by the URL http://localhost/home.aspx?q=sitecore., the URL rendering will request the URL http://www.google.com/search?q=sitecore.

member.summary: Gets a pipe separated list of URL prefixes to ignore when mapping friendly URLs.

remarks.para: Normally, URL requests coming in are mapped to an item and the request is redirected to the items layout page.

For example, if the item /home/news. has the layout /layouts/newslist.aspx., the URL http://localhost/home/news.aspx. will be redirected to http://localhost/layouts/newslist.aspx?path=[id of the News item].
To prevent this redirection to take place for physical aspx pages, their prefixes can be added to .
For example, if an aspx page called /forms/registration.aspx. existed, the prefix /forms/ could be added to web.config to prevent requests for this page to be redirected.
Elements must be lowercase and non-empty.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.BulkUpdateContext.DescendantsRebuildThreshold
member.summary:
Gets the descendants rebuild threshold.
Under active BulkUpdateContext, table Descendants is not updated, but all operations are enqueued to be performed when leaving the BulkUpdateContext. The setting is used to check if number of the operations exceeds the value of the setting, then full descendants rebuild is performed; otherwise, the enqueued operations are executed. Default value: 1000. In order to change the setting's value, add setting "BulkUpdateContext.DescendantsRebuildThreshold" with your custom value into configuration.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.LanguageFallback.AllowVaryFallbackSettingsPerLanguage
member.summary:
If set to 'true', then values from both versioned 'Enable Language Fallback' and shared 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox fields on the field definition item are used to determine whether language fallback functionality should be enabled for the corresponding field. It allows you to have different fallback settings for the same field in different content languages.
Example: when 'en-CA' tries to fallback to 'en', the checkbox field will be retrieved from the field definition item in 'en-CA', thus such version should exist. If retrieved value is 'false', then the 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox field is used.
Note: enabling this feature has negative impact on performance.
If set to 'false', only the shared 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox field on the field definition item is used to determine whether language fallback functionality should be enabled for the corresponding field.
Default value: false.
member.value: true if allow vary fallback settings per language; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.LanguageFallback.AllowStandardValuesForSharedLanguageFallback
member.summary:
If set to 'true' will allow 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' checkbox inheriting Standard Values of the base 'Template Field' template. In general, this allows switching the 'Enable Shared Language Fallback' setting for all field together by specifying the value on on the Standard Values 'Template Field'.
Default value: false.
member.value: true if allow Standard Values for EnableSharedLanguageFallback; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.Settings.Media.DefaultImageBackgroundColor
member.summary: Gets the default background color for dynamically resizing images to different aspect ratios than the originals.
member.remarks:
Sitecore applies this background color only for image types that do not support transparency (image/jpeg, image/gif and image/bmp). When resizing any other image types (including image/png), Sitecore always applies a transparent background.
You can specify a color name (such as Black or Red) or a hex color code (such as #CE55E2).
If you specify no value, Sitecore applies a black background color when resizing such images.
member.value: The color of the image background. Default value: Color.Empty.

summary.para: Sitecore maintains a state about the current webpage (in the collection) and about the current session (in the collection).
Typical information include the current user, the current web item, the current master item, the current layout etc.
The State class encapsulates both the Items and Session collections.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.AddRenderings
member.summary: Gets an array list of renderings to add to the default list of renderings.

remarks.para: As the web engine renders a page, it builds a list of renderings to add to the page. Normally the renderings are fetched from the current item, but the AddRenderings State variable allows additional renderings to be rendered on the page.
Usually this is used in global.aspx to programatically add new renderings to a page based on certain conditions.
The list consists of either IDs or names of renderings.
The scope of the value is page and it is stored in the Items variable "SC_ADD_RENDERINGS".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.ClientLanguage
member.summary: Gets or sets the ISO language code the the current client language.
member.value: The current client language ISO code.

remarks.para: The client language is the language that the Sitecore client is presented in. For instance if the client language is "da" the client will present all menus, toolbars etc. in the Danish language.
The client language code is usually set when the user logs in. The language code for a user is specified in the Client Language field on the __User template.
If the language code is changed, the Sitecore client must be reloaded in order to retrieve the new language from the server.
The scope of the value is session and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_CLIENT_LANGUAGE".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.CommitDisabled
member.summary: Option to disable commits on items.
member.value: true if commits are disabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: The scope of the value is thread and it is stored in the thread variable "SC_COMMIT_DISABLED".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.ContentDatabase
member.summary: Gets or sets the content database.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.CustomLayout
member.summary: Gets or sets the ID or name of a custom layout to use for the current page request.
member.value: The ID or name of the custom layout.

remarks.para: The default layout can be overridden by setting the custom layout before the web engine starts (typically in Page_Init or a page handler). This can be used to build the layout programatically in conjunction with and .
The scope of the value is page and it is stored in the Items variable "SC_CUSTOM_LAYOUT".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.DebugMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if Sitecore is in debug mode.
member.value: True, if Sitecore is in debug mode, otherwise false.

remarks.para: DebugMode is the global controller of all debug activities. It controls such tools as Profiling, Trace, Rendering Borders and Rendering Info. Only if DebugMode is true will these tools be available.
The DebugMode flag also adds further information on the Debug tab in the content area.
The DebugMode flag can be enabled by specifying the "sc_debug=1" argument on the query string. To disable it, specify "sc_debug=0".
The scope of the value is sesion and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_DEBUGMODE".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.Desktop
member.summary: Gets or sets the path of the client desktop webpage.
member.value: The path to the webpage that specifies the Sitecore client.

remarks.para: A desktop is the basic webpage that contains a Sitecore client. Sitecore only provides one desktop, but customers or partners may implement other desktops.
The desktop is initialized during user login. When the login procedure has completed, the browser is redirected to the desktop webpage.
The desktop for a specific user is specified in the Desktop field on the __User template. This is a lookup field pointing to "/sitecore/system/Desktops and Themes/Desktops".
If the user item does not specify a desktop, the value from is used.
The scope of the value is session and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_DESKTOP".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.DisableDefaultRenderings
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if the default renderings are disabled or not.
member.value: True, if default renderings are disabled, otherwise false.

remarks.para: Default renderings are the renderings, specified as part of the current layout. For instance the Home layout may have a Document rendering.
When builing a programatic layout using and , it is possible to disable any renderings that the layout specifies.
The scope of the value is page and it stored in the Items variable "SC_DISABLE_DEFAULT_RENDERINGS".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.DisableItemChangeRegistering
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates of item changes are registered.
member.value: true if the disables the item change registering; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: The scope of the value is thread and it is stored in the thread variable "SC_COMMIT_DISABLED".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.DispatchEvents
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if events are dispatched.
member.value: True, if events are dispatched, otherwise false.

remarks.para: The event dispatcher is the event handling mechanism in Sitecore. Certain actions raise events, for instance saving an item, publishing, tracing and exception handling.
This flag can be used to disable event handling on the current web page.
The scope of the value is page and it is stored in the Items variable "SC_DISPATCH_EVENTS".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.DrawRenderingBorders
member.summary: Get or sets a boolean that indicates if borders are drawn around renderings.
member.value: True, if is true and borders are drawn, otherwise false.

remarks.para: When the web engine is running in debug mode, it can drawn borders around each rendering. This makes it easy for the developer to identify individual renderings.
This flag requires that is true.
The scope of the value is session and it stored in the Session variable "SC_DRAW_RENDERING_BORDERS".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.ExtensionObjects
member.summary: Gets the hash list of XSL extention objects.
member.value: A hash list of extention objects.

remarks.para: An XSL extention is an object that is accessible from within XSL transformations. For instance the XslHelper object, which implements the "sc:fld" function.
The developer may make more extention objects available on a per page basis. It such case the new extention object can be added to this list.
The scope of this list is page only. To add extention objects globally, use the xslExtentions section ion the web.config.
The ExtensionObjects is usually used in global.aspx.
The scope of the value is page and it is stored in the Items variable "SC_EXPAND_LINKED_DATABASES".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.Form
member.summary: Gets or sets the current form collection from web page.
member.value: The form collection from the current web page.

remarks.para: The Sitecore request handler (HttpModule) overrides the current form collection in order to find the correct layout for the page. The normal form collection () is therefore not valid. However Sitecore stores the original form collection in this variable before overwriting it.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.Language
member.summary: Get or sets the current language code.

remarks.para: The current language specifies which pieces of content, Sitecore fetches by default. For instance if the language code is "da" (Danish), Sitecore will by default fetch contents that have the code "da".
The code is just an identifier, but usually it is an ISO language code, e.g. "en", "en-us", "da", "ge" etc.
This State variable does not change the language of the Sitecore client.

member.example:
The following example changes the language to german.
string english = version.GetFieldValue("Text"); // english text State.Language = "ge"; string german = version.GetFieldValue("Text"); // german text

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.LastError
member.summary: Gets a hash list of sections containing the last errors.
member.value: A hash list of of errors.
member.remarks: It is possible to log errors using this State variable. The key of the error identifies the type of error, e.g. "Extranet".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.MasterItem
member.summary: Gets or sets the current master item.

remarks.para: The current master item is used in the Sitecore client. It points to the current loaded item in the content area and is set when the content area page loads.
The scope of the value is page and it is stored the Items variable "SC_CURRENT_MASTER_ITEM".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.PreviewDate
member.summary: Gets or sets the current date/time of a preview.

remarks.para: When a preview is generated, it reflects the web site at a certain date and time. This date and time is specified in this State variable.

member.summary: Gets or sets the current publishing groups of a preview.
member.value: The publishing groups of the preview.

member.value: true if the system is previewing; otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.Profiling
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if profiling data are generated.
member.value: True, if is true and profiling is enabled, otherwise false.

remarks.para: When profiling the web engine times each rendering. This information is available on the Sitecore debug pages "http://www.mysite.net/sitecore/debug".
Profiling can only be enabled if is true.
The scope of the value is session and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_PROFILING".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.RemoveRenderings
member.summary: Gets a has array list of renderings that should be removed from the list of default renderings.
member.value: An array list of rendering names or IDs.

remarks.para: Default renderings are the renderings specified as part of the current layout. For instance the Home layout may have a Document rendering.
When builing a programatic layout using and , it is possible to remove default renderings.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.ResetAfterWebView
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if the web editing state should be reset after web view.
member.value: True, if it should be reset, otherwise false.
member.remarks: This is for internal use only.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.ShowEditDots
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if dots (and panel) are shown in preview and web edit mode.
member.value: True, if dots are shown, otherwise false.

remarks.para: Dots are the small markers that an editor clicks on in preview or web edit mode to edit the content.
The dots can be turned off. For example this is done in the Web view pane in the Sitecore client.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.ShowRenderingInfo
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if rendering info is available.
member.value: True, if is true and rendering info should be available, otherwise false.

remarks.para: The web engine can render information about each rendering on the web page. That makes it easy for a developer to identify the individual renderings and their parameters.
Rendering information can only be enabled if is true.
The scope of the value is session and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_SHOW_RENDERING_INFO".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.Theme
member.summary: Gets or sets the current theme.
member.value: The name of the current theme.

remarks.para: A theme is the appearance of the Sitecore client. Themes control the stylesheet and images used in the client.
The theme is initialized during user login.
The desktop for a specific user is specified in the Theme field on the __User template. This is a lookup field pointing to "/sitecore/system/Desktops and Themes/Themes".
If the user item does not specify a theme, the value from is used.
The scope of the value is session and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_THEME".

member.name: P:Sitecore.Configuration.State.Tracing
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean that indicates if tracing data is collected.
member.value: True, if is true and tracing is enabled, otherwise false.

remarks.para: When tracing the web engine collects information about the rendering process. This information is available on the Sitecore debug pages "http://www.mysite.net/sitecore/debug".
Tracing can only be enabled if is true.
The scope of the value is session and it is stored in the Session variable "SC_TRACING".

member.value: The identified by the "path" query string parameter, or null if the item was not found.

remarks.para: The current item is the context item from which the web page is rendered. For instance if the current item points to the Home item, the web engine will render the layout associated with the Home item.
The current web item is by default obtained by parsing the Path argument on the request query string.
The scope of the value is page and it is stored in the Items variable sc_CurrentItem.

members.member:
=============================================================== Implements a utility class for handling and executing SQL statements.
The class is aimed at SQL Servers and uses the native .NET driver for optimal performance. This class will not work with other databases.
Normally only the AddParameter, AddWhereClause and Execute methods are called. The other methods function as utility methods for these methods.
The following code deletes the company "Alfreds Futterkiste" from the Customers table.
SqlBuilder builder = new SqlBuilder("Customers", SqlStatementType.Delete); builder.AddWhereClause("CompanyName='Alfreds Futterkiste'"); builder.Execute(myConnectionString);
===============================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates an SQL command object from a connection object. An SQL connection string. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
Important: Remember to close the connection after using the returned command object (cmd). Use cmd.Connection.Close().
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates an SQL command object from a connection object. An SQL connection object. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates an SQL Delete command object. An SQL command object. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates an SQL Insert command object. An SQL command object. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates a Stored Procedure command object. An SQL command object. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates a User Defined Function command object. An SQL command object. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Creates an Update command object. An SQL command object. The created SQL command object.
This method is called by the Execute method. It is rarely used seperately.
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Executes an SQL command statement. A string containing an SQL statement. A SQL Server connection string.
The SQL command statement can be an Insert, Delete or Update statement. The result from the command is discarded. ---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Executes an SQL command statement. A string containing an SQL statement. A SQL Server connection string. Time before the command times out.
The SQL command statement can be an Insert, Delete or Update statement. The result from the command is discarded.
SqlUtil.ExecCommand("delete * from customers", myConnection);
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Extracts a value from a connection string. Name of the value to extract. A connection string. The value of the named parameter. If not found, blank is returned.
string connectionString = "data source=myserver;user id=guest;password=;initial catalog=northwind;Connect Timeout=30"; string userID = SqlUtil.ExtractConnnectionValue("user id"); // guest
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Gets an array of results from an SQL statement. A string containing an SQL statement. A SQL Server connection string.
An array of results from the query.
ArrayList result = SqlUtil.GetArray("select CompanyName from Customers", "data source=myserver;user id=guest;password=;initial catalog=northwind;Connect Timeout=30");
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Gets a row count for a table. Name of the table. An SQL where clause. A connection string.
The number of rows in the table. The condition is specified without the "where" keyword.
int count = SqlUtil.GetCount("customers", "Country='Germany'", "data source=myserver;user id=guest;password=;initial catalog=northwind;Connect Timeout=30");
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Gets a Dataset object from an SQL statement. A string containing an SQL statement. A connection string. Starting position for the Dataset object. Max number of rows. The created Dataset object.
The following example gets the first 100 customers from the Customers table.
Dataset dataset = SqlUtil.GetDataset("select * from customers", "data source=myserver;user id=guest;password=;initial catalog=northwind;Connect Timeout=30", 0, 100);
---------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------- Gets results from an SQL statement as a hashtable. A string containing an SQL statement. A SQL Server connection string. ---------------------------------------------------------------

member.name: T:Sitecore.Data.Items.ItemPathType
member.summary:
Specifies which item information shall be used during item path construction.
Example: A path to an item can be constructed from , , , or . provides a language-specific item path, meaning one item can have many display name paths.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Items.ItemPathType.ItemID
member.summary:
Path is constructed from IDs.
Example path to 'home' item: '/{11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111}/{0DE95AE4-41AB-4D01-9EB0-67441B7C2450}/{110D559F-DEA5-42EA-9C1C-8A5DF7E70EF9}'

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Items.ItemPathType.Key
member.summary:
Path is constructed from keys (lowercase name).
Example: '/sitecore/content/home/sample item'

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Items.ItemPathType.Name
member.summary:
Path is constructed from item names.
Example:'/sitecore/content/Home/Sample Item'

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Items.ItemPathType.DisplayName
member.summary:
Path is constructed from display names. Display name path is language-specific, so one item can have multiple display paths.
Example for English: '/sitecore/Content/Home/Sample Item'
Example for Danish: '/sitecore/content/Hjem/Sample Item'

member.name: M:Sitecore.Data.Serialization.Yaml.Storage.YamlFileSystemTree.GetTargetPhysicalPath(Sitecore.Abstractions.Serialization.IItemData)
member.summary:
CALCULATING AN ITEM'S PATH TO SAVE TO, GIVEN A WHOLE ITEM WITH PARENT ID, VIRTUAL PATH 1. Start by using "finding file paths, given a virtual path" on the parent path of the item 2. If no matches exist, throw - parent must be serialized 3. If multiple matches exist, narrow them by the parent ID of the item - if no matches, throw 4. If one match, parent path is found 4.5. Determine if this item has any name-dupes in the source store (use 'finding child paths, given a physical path', and filter on the same name prefix). - If no (and no can include 'yes, but this item exists and has an unescaped name already so we want to reuse that'), push its name onto the path string. - If yes, escape it and push that onto the path string
5. Strip characters not allowed by the filesystem from the base path 6. The path string is now the 'base' path, which may be too long to use 7. Determine if the base-string is over-length (which would be 240-$(Serialization.SerializationFolderPathMaxLength)) - If the base string is short enough, return it
8. If it's over length create a folder named the parent ID in the root folder, and put it there

member.name: M:Sitecore.Data.Serialization.Yaml.Storage.YamlFileSystemTree.GetPhysicalFilePathsForVirtualPath(System.String)
member.summary: Gets the physical file paths for virtual path. 1. Break apart the virtual path into components 2. Beginning with the physical SFS root, drill down the virtual path components (use 'finding child paths, given a physical path') - At each level, look for all possible item names (item.yml and item_2342434.yml) - If multiple are present, follow ALL paths down 3. If an expected child path is not present, stop searching down the current path 4. Once all possible paths have been searched down, return files that matched the path 5. Note: this means that if there are two /foo items with children named 'bar', and you get /foo/bar by path, you'll get BOTH bar items even though different parents. Paths match, bro. Sitecore API would pick one of the foos and give only one child, fwiw.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Data.Serialization.Yaml.Storage.YamlFileSystemTree.GetChildPaths(Sitecore.Abstractions.Serialization.IItemMetadata)
member.summary: Gets the child file paths. 1. Determine the physical path of the item to get children for (use 'finding file paths, given a virtual path'), compare matches against ID 2. Determine if Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(filename) exists as a directory in the physical path 3. If it does, get all children of that directory that are both files and have the expected serialized item extension from the formatter 4. Read the parent item file and get the item ID.Check in the SFS root for a folder named that ID (a loopback with children of the item whose names were too long to fit) - If the folder exists, add all children of that directory that are both files and have the expected serialized item extension from the formatter 5. Note: unlike searching by path, this guarantees ONLY children of the correct item if multiple same named items are present

member.name: T:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3
member.summary: Represents the state of a transfer operation in version 3 of the transfer API.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3.Unknown
member.summary: State is unknown, which means that the transfer operation has not started yet or the state cannot be determined.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3.InProgress
member.summary: State indicates that the transfer operation is currently in progress, which means that it has started and is actively transferring data.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3.Finished
member.summary: Finished state indicates that the transfer operation has completed successfully, which means that all data has been transferred without errors.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3.Failed
member.summary: Failed state indicates that the transfer operation has completed with errors, which means that some or all data may not have been transferred successfully.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3.Queued
member.summary: Queued state indicates that the transfer operation is waiting to be processed, which means that it has been scheduled but has not started yet.

member.name: F:Sitecore.Data.Transfer.TransferStateV3.Discarded
member.summary: Indicates that the item has been discarded and is no longer available for use.

===============================================================
Helper functions for use with xsl files.
The public functions in this class can be called from an xsl file by using the sc prefix (ex. sc:fld(...))
===============================================================

---------------------------------------------------------------
Initialize an sql connection
Database connection string Empty string <xsl:value-of select="sql:connect(sc:GetApppSetting('myconnection'))"/> ---------------------------------------------------------------

---------------------------------------------------------------
Perform a full text search
Words to search for (Google style) Table to search Comma separated list of fields to include in result
Empty string <xsl:value-of select="sql:fullsearch('release road map', 'title, description', 0, 20)"/> ---------------------------------------------------------------

---------------------------------------------------------------
Perform a full text search
Words to search for (Google style) Table to search Comma separated list of fields to include in result Page to show (starts from 0)
Number of records per page (if zero, all records will be shown) Empty string <xsl:value-of select="sql:fullsearch('release road map', 'title, description', 0, 20)"/> ---------------------------------------------------------------

member.name: M:Sitecore.Xml.Xsl.SqlHelper.GetShortId(System.String)
member.summary: Gets a short id from an ordinary id.

members.member:
---------------------------------------------------------------
Move to next record in current dataset
True if position was advanced, false otherwise <xsl:value-of select="sql:movenext()"/> ---------------------------------------------------------------

---------------------------------------------------------------
Enter page mode (restrict data to a certain page index)
Page to show (starts from 0) Number of records per page (if zero, all records will be shown) Empty string <xsl:value-of select="sql:select('SELECT * FROM Products', 0, 20)"/> ---------------------------------------------------------------

---------------------------------------------------------------
Get number of pages given a page size
Number of pages needed to show entire recordset <xsl:value-of select="sql:pagecount(20)"/> ---------------------------------------------------------------

For instance, the content of an image field may look like this: In this example the available subvalues are 'src' and 'alt'. Assuming that the field containg the data is called Banner image, the following example will extract the image source for use in an image tag:
member.param:
Xml node containing the document (item).
To represent the current item in the xsl, pass . in this parameter (ex. sc:fld('menu image',.,'src')).
For other items, pass the xpath of the item (ex. sc:fld('content image',item[@key='about'],'src') will show the subvalue src of the field called Content image in the child document called About. To access the parent document use ..)

member.name: T:Sitecore.DateUtil
member.summary: Implements a utility class for manipulating dates.
member.remarks: The DateUtil operates on ISO formatted date/times for the most part. An ISO formatted date/time string is formatted as yyyyMMddTHHmmss.

member.name: P:Sitecore.DateUtil.IsoNow
member.summary: Gets the current time formatted as ISO date/time string.
member.value: Now formatted as a ISO formatted date/time string.
member.remarks: The date/time string is formatted as "yyyyMMddTHHmmss".
member.example:
The following example sets isoNow to now in ISO format.
string isoNow = DateUtil.IsoNow;

member.name: P:Sitecore.DateUtil.IsoNowDate
member.summary: Gets the current date formatted as ISO date string.
member.value: Now formatted as a ISO formatted date string.
member.remarks: The date string is formatted as "yyyyMMdd".
member.example:
The following example sets isoNow to the current date in ISO format.
string isoNow = DateUtil.IsoNowDate;

member.name: P:Sitecore.DateUtil.IsoNowTime
member.summary: Gets the current time formatted as ISO time string.
member.value: Now formatted as a ISO formatted time string.
member.remarks: The time string is formatted as "HHmmss".
member.example:
The following example sets isoNow to the current time in ISO format.
string isoNow = DateUtil.IsoNowTime;

member.name: P:Sitecore.DateUtil.IsoNowWithTicks
member.summary: Gets the current time formatted as ISO date/time string with ticks appended.
member.value: Now formatted as a ISO formatted date/time string.
member.remarks: The date/time string is formatted as "yyyyMMddTHHmmss" and ":{ticks}" is appended.
member.example:
The following example sets isoNow to now in ISO format.
string isoNow = DateUtil.IsoNowWithTicks; // might return 20012008T102817:2382193728213

member.name: P:Sitecore.DateUtil.TicksPerMillisecond
member.summary: Gets the number of ticks per millisecond.

member.name: M:Sitecore.DateUtil.Compare(System.DateTime,System.DateTime)
member.summary: Compares two instances of System.DateTime and returns an integer that indicates whether the first instance is earlier than, the same as, or later than the second instance.
member.returns: A signed number indicating the relative values of t1 and t2. Less than zero: t1 is earlier than t2. Zero: t1 is the same as t2. Greater than zero: t1 is later than t2.

member.name: M:Sitecore.DateUtil.EnsureDatesCanBeCompared(System.DateTime[])
member.summary: Ensures that dates can be compared.
member.exception: Exception is thrown if dates are not equal to or and dates have different kinds.

member.name: M:Sitecore.DateUtil.CompareDatesIgnoringSeconds(System.DateTime,System.DateTime)
member.summary: Compares two instances of System.DateTime and returns an integer that indicates whether the first instance is earlier than, the same as, or later than the second instance. Seconds of System.DateTime instances are ignored during the comparison.
member.returns: A signed number indicating the relative values of t1 and t2. Less than zero: t1 is earlier than t2. Zero: t1 is the same as t2. Greater than zero: t1 is later than t2.

members.member:
=============================================================== Implements a class that encapsulates the operating system high resolution timer using native API functions.
This class is usually used for profiling.
The class uses the API functions QueryPerformanceCounter and QueryPerformanceFrequency.
===============================================================

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the HighResTimer class.
member.remarks: The timer is not started automatically.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.#ctor(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the HighResTimer class.
member.param: A boolean indicating if the timer should be started.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.ElapsedTimeSpan
member.summary: Gets the elapsed time as a .

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.SecondsElapsed
member.summary: Gets the number of seconds that has elapsed since the timer was started.
member.returns: Number of seconds since the timer was started.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.Elapsed
member.summary: Gets the number of milliseconds that has elapsed since the timer was started.
member.returns: Number of milliseconds since the timer was started.
member.remarks: Stops the timer.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.ElapsedTicks
member.summary: Gets the number of ticks that has elapsed since the timer was started.
member.returns: Number of ticks since the timer was started.
member.remarks: Stops the timer.

example.code: HighResTimer timer = new HighResTimer(true); double ms = timer.ElapsedTicks();

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.GetElapsed
member.summary: Gets the number of milliseconds that has elapsed since the timer was started.
member.returns: Number of milliseconds since the timer was started.
member.remarks: Does not stop the timer.

example.code: HighResTimer timer = new HighResTimer(true); double ms = timer.GetElapsed();

member.name: M:Sitecore.Diagnostics.HighResTimer.Supported
member.summary: Checks if timers is supported by the operating system.
member.returns: True, if the operating system supports timers, otherwise false.

member.returns: Returns 1.0 divided by the timer frequency.

summary.para: The queued event used to propagate an event data from one Sitecore instance to others in scaled environments.
Carries a serialized representation of an action with additional metadata (like , ).
An action is de-serialized, and replayed on a local instance. Example: Item saved remote event is used to remove obsolete data from cache layer.
Check API for more details.

Acceptable formats: empty string - default domain from specified database in parameter. database_name: - default domain in specified database. :domain_name - domain with specified name in database specified in parameter. :domain_id - domain with specified ID (id of dictionary domain item) in database specified in parameter. domain_name - domain with specified name in database specified in parameter. domain_id - domain with specified ID (id of dictionary domain item) in database specified in parameter. database_name:domain_name - domain with specified name in specified database. database_name:domain_id - domain with specified id in specified database.

member.summary: Uses the lpTargetPath string as is. Otherwise, it is converted from an MS-DOS path to a path.

member.name: F:Sitecore.IO.VirtualDrive.DDD_REMOVE_DEFINITION
member.summary: Removes the specified definition for the specified device. To determine which definition to remove, the function walks the list of mappings for the device, looking for a match of lpTargetPath against a prefix of each mapping associated with this device. The first mapping that matches is the one removed, and then the function returns. If lpTargetPath is NULL or a pointer to a NULL string, the function will remove the first mapping associated with the device and pop the most recent one pushed. If there is nothing left to pop, the device name will be removed. If this value is not specified, the string pointed to by the lpTargetPath parameter will become the new mapping for this device.

Links a language/version specific item field to another item language/version with specific value (path).
Example: First version of 'Home' item in 'DA' language has 'Text' field that has a link to 'About' item in first version of 'DA' language.
Each link stores information about source and target items:
Source item: , , , , .
Target item: , , , , . Must take into account source field language/version configuration - no need to save item language/version details if the link is produced from shared field. No need to save item version info if source field is un-versioned.

member.name: M:Sitecore.MainUtil.CreateObject(System.String,System.String,System.Object[])
member.summary: Creates an instance of an object.
member.returns: The instantiated object or null if the object could not be instantiated.
member.remarks:
The assembly name is expanded to a qualified path by:
prepending "/bin/", if the filename does not contain any folder information.
appending ".dll", if the filename does not end with ".dll".
If the object could not be instantiated, an error message is written to the log file (usually located in the data folder).

example.code: object MyObject = MainUtil.CreateObject("/bin/MyAssembly.dll", "MyNamespace.MyObject"); object MyObject2 = MainUtil.CreateObject("MyAssembly", "MyNamespace.MyObject2", parameter1, parameter2);

member.remarks: Only the values 'true' or 'false' are recognized. For all other values, the default will be returned. The comparison is case-insensitive.

example.code: bool b0 = MainUtil.StringToBool("True", true); // true bool b1 = MainUtil.StringToBool("false", true); // false bool b0 = MainUtil.StringToBool("", true); // true bool b0 = MainUtil.StringToBool("abc", false); // false bool b0 = MainUtil.StringToBool("yes", false); // false bool b0 = MainUtil.StringToBool("1", false); // false

member.name: M:Sitecore.MainUtil.Substring(System.String,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Retrieves a substring from a string. The substring starts at a specified character position and has a specified length.
member.param: The index of the start of the substring.
The number of characters in the substring.
member.returns: A String equivalent to the substring of length length that begins at start in the string.
member.remarks: No exception is thrown if length is greater than the length of the string.

example.code: string text = MainUtil.Substring("Hello world", 6, 100); // "world" string text = MainUtil.Substring("Hello world", 2, 3); // "llo"

member.name: M:Sitecore.MainUtil.Substring(System.String,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Gets a substring of maximum length of a string.
member.param: The number of characters in the substring.
If true, three dots are appended to the substring.
member.returns: A subtring starting at zero and ending a max characters of the string.
member.remarks: No exception is thrown if max is greater than the length of the string.

example.code: string text = MainUtil.Substring("Hello world", 6, true); // "Hel..." string text = MainUtil.Substring("Hello world", 6, false); // "Hello "

member.name: T:Sitecore.Web.UI.Pages.DialogForm
member.summary: Provides a class that handles dialog forms.

remarks.para: The class has methods that handles OK and Cancel button clicks. the methods can be overridden to provide other functionality.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.UI.Pages.DialogForm.OnLoad(System.EventArgs)
member.param: The instance containing the event data.
member.remarks: This method notifies the server control that it should perform actions common to each HTTP request for the page it is associated with, such as setting up a database query. At this stage in the page lifecycle, server controls in the hierarchy are created and initialized, view state is restored, and form controls reflect client-side data. Use the IsPostBack property to determine whether the page is being loaded in response to a client postback, or if it is being loaded and accessed for the first time.

member.name: T:Sitecore.Web.UI.Sheer.ClientPage
member.summary: Represents an .aspx file, also known as a Web Forms page, requested from a server that hosts an ASP.NET Web application.

remarks.para: The ClientPage class is associated with files that have an .aspx extension. These files are compiled at run time as Page objects and cached in server memory.
The ClientPage class extends the Page base class in several ways.

If you want to create a Web Forms page using the code-behind technique, derive from this class. Rapid application development (RAD) designers, such as Visual Studio .NET, automatically use this model to create Web Forms pages.

The Page object serves as the naming container for all server controls in a page, except those that implement the INamingContainer interface, or are children of controls that implement this interface.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Web.UI.Sheer.ClientPage.IsEvent
member.summary: Gets a value that indicates if the page is running in Event or Result mode.
member.value: True, if the page is in Event or Result mode, otherwise false.

remarks.para: The property is set to true, if the current request contains a field with the name "__ISEVENT" and the value "1". This field is sent to the server when Sheer initiates an event.
The property is also true, when Sheer posts a result to the server.
The property is false, when the page is loading as part of a normal ASP.NET page load.

This property is usually used in WebControl OnLoad or OnPreRender methods to determine if dynamic controls should be created. The dynamic control are only created when IsEvent is false. When IsEvent is true, Sheer will create all the dynamic control automatically and there is no need for the controls to do it again.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Web.UI.Sheer.ClientPage.IsResult
member.summary: Gets a value that indicates if the page is running in Result mode.
member.value: True, if the page is in Result mode, otherwise false.

remarks.para: The property is set to true, if the current request contains a field with the name "__RESULT". This field is sent to the server when Sheer posts a result.
The property is false, when Sheer has posted an event or the page is loading as part of a normal ASP.NET page load.
This property is usually used in pipelines to determine if the user has posted a response.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Web.UI.Sheer.ClientPage.Modified
member.summary: Gets a value that indicates if the fields on page has been modified.
member.value: True, if the fields has been changed, otherwise false.
member.remarks: This value is posted from the client and can be set on the server. If set on the server, the value is transfered to the client.

member.name: P:Sitecore.Web.UI.Sheer.ClientPage.PersistViewStateToClient
member.summary: Gets a value that indicates if ViewState should be persisted on the client in the __VIEWSTATE field.
member.value: True, if the ViewState is persisted on the client, otherwise false.

remarks.para: When PersistViewStateToClient is true, the ViewState is sent to the client and stored in the field "__VIEWSTATE".
When PersistViewStateToClient is false, the ViewState is persisted using an object that is specified in the web.config and implements the IViewStateStore interface.

member.name: T:Sitecore.Web.UI.Sheer.ClientPipelineArgs
member.summary: Represents the arguments to a pipeline.

remarks.para: Pipeline arguments contain context and state information about a pipeline, e.g. the the of processors and any parameters.
An object of this type is passed to every method as part of a pipeline.

The WaitForPostBack method suspends the pipeline after the current processor has completed and wait for the user to post a response. When the user responds the IsPostBack property is true. The value of the response is located in the Result property.
You can create an inherited class to hold your own values.

member.name: T:Sitecore.Web.IPageHandler
member.remarks: A page handler is registered in web.config under the <pageHandlers> section
member.example:
The following example shows how a page handler might be registered in web.config
<pageHandlers> <handler mode="on" name="Statistics" assembly="Sitecore.Kernel" type="Sitecore.Logging" expectedResult="" /> </pageHandlers>
The attributes of the <handler> tag is:
mode=on|off - Determines if the handler is active. Inactive handlers are never called
name=name - Descriptive name of the page handler. This value is not used by Sitecore, but might be useful for people reading web.config
assembly=name - Name of assembly containing the page handler class. This value is case-sensitive
type=name - Type name of the page handler class. This value is case-sensitive
expectedResult=value - This is the expected return value of the page handler method. If the return value is different, an error message will be sent to the current PageTrace.
The page handler is free to add additional attributes if this is needed. All attributes of the <handler> tag are passed to the method.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.IPageHandler.Execute(System.Collections.Specialized.NameValueCollection)
member.summary: This method is called whenever a page is being generated
member.returns: A status message that is compared to the value of 'expectedResult' from web.config.
member.remarks: The call is being made during the Init phase of the page life cycle

member.name: T:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller
member.remarks:
Admin-only endpoints to explore, upload, validate, consume, inspect, retry and discard content transfer sources coming from the file system or Azure Blob Storage. Responses commonly include hypermedia actions via an Actions dictionary (built by ) to guide next operations.
Key concepts:
Source types: file:// (file system) and blob:// (Azure Blob Storage). See and .
States: transfer state (e.g., Queued, InProgress, Failed) and blob state (e.g., Uploaded, Consumed, Error).
Paging: 1-based; default page size is 50 for item listings and history.
Security: with admin-only access; CORS via policy "ContentTransferCorsPolicy".
Exposed operations:
— discover available sources and next actions.
— upload a gzip (default) or raw stream to blob storage.
— start consuming a file:// or blob:// source into a database.
/ — inspect overall and per‑source status.
— review recent consumed sources across databases.
/ — browse and inspect items in a consumed source.
— check a blob’s current state and related info.
— retry a failed source; — discard a source and its data.
Examples:
Check blob state: GET …/GetBlobState?fileName=content_2025-08-28.raif
Consume uploaded blob: GET …/ConsumeFile?databaseName=master&fileName=blob://content_2025-08-28.raif

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.History(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.remarks: Returns a paged list of recently consumed transfer sources aggregated across all Sitecore databases. Each entry includes the consumed source name, original file name, consume date, merge strategy, and state change events. Paging is 1-based. Use and to navigate.
member.param: 1-based page number. Must be greater than 0. Default: 1.
Items per page. Must be greater than 0. Default: 50.
member.returns: 200 OK with when paging arguments are valid; 400 Bad Request when or is less than 1.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/History?page=1&pageSize=50

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.Retry(System.String,System.String)
member.remarks: If the source is still loaded in memory, its state is reset and the transfer resumes. Otherwise, the source will be re-consumed. Only sources in the Failed state can be retried.
member.param: The consumed source name or original file name.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/Retry?databaseName=master&fileName=consumed_2025-08-28_12-00-00Z

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.Discard(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Discard a source and its associated data.
member.remarks: Deletes the file from the file system (if present), clears transfer status, and deletes the blob and auxiliary blobs. Loaded-in-memory sources cannot be discarded. If the consumed source name is used, its state changes to Discarded.
member.param: The consumed source name or original file name to discard.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/Discard?databaseName=master&fileName=content_2025-08-28.raif

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.ItemDetails(System.String,System.String,System.Guid)
member.summary: Get details for a specific item within a consumed source.
member.remarks:
Returns the item's definition (IDs, name, template, parent, timestamps) and field data. Fields are represented as:
for versioned, language-specific fields.
for language-only fields (no version).
for shared/unversioned fields (no language/version).
The source must be consumed prior to calling this endpoint.
member.returns: 200 OK with when the item is found; 404 Not Found when the item or source cannot be resolved.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/ItemDetails?databaseName=master&sourceName=consumed_2025-08-28_12-00-00Z&itemId=11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.ListItems(System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: List items contained in a consumed source.
member.remarks: Returns a paged list of items with minimal details. Use actions in the response to navigate: "NextPage"/"PreviousPage" for paging and "ItemDetails" to fetch full details for a specific item.
member.param: 1-based page number. Must be 1 or greater. Default: 1.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/ListItems?databaseName=master&sourceName=consumed_2025-08-28_12-00-00Z&page=2

member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/Status

member.summary: Get detailed status for a specific consumed source.
member.remarks: Returns item counts, states, strategy, and validation errors (if any) for the specified consumed source. The response includes actions to list items for the source and to navigate back to overall status.

member.summary: Get the current state of a transfer blob or original file.

member.summary: Upload a transfer file stream to Azure Blob Storage.
member.remarks: If is false (default), the request body is expected to be gzip-compressed and will be decompressed server-side. Otherwise, the content is uploaded as-is. On success, a small JSON payload is returned for convenience.

Set to true to upload the content without gzip decompression.
member.example: POST /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/UploadBlob?blobName=content_2025-08-28.raif

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.Explore
member.remarks: Returns a mixed list of file system sources (per writable database) and blob storage sources, along with actions to consume, discard, retry (when applicable), or view status details. File system entries may show "Uploading" or "Error" when marked by the status provider.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/Explore

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV2Controller.ConsumeFile(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Consume a file or blob into a database.
member.remarks:
Starts an asynchronous consumption process for the given resource. The must be prefixed with:
file:// for a file located under the transfer root path for the specified database.
blob:// for an uploaded blob in Azure Blob Storage.
Returns HTTP 202 (Accepted) when the background process is started.
member.param: The file name with schema prefix (file:// or blob://).
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v2/ItemsTransfer/ConsumeFile?databaseName=master&fileName=blob://content_2025-08-28.raif

member.remarks:
Admin-only REST endpoints to explore, upload, validate, consume, inspect, retry and discard content transfer sources coming from the file system or Azure Blob Storage. Responses commonly include standard ResultV3 objects or HTTP status codes.
Key concepts:
Source types: file system files and Azure Blob Storage blobs.
States: transfer state (e.g., Queued, InProgress, Failed) and blob state (e.g., Uploaded, Consumed, Error).
Paging: 1-based; default page size is 50 for item listings and history.
Security: with admin-only access or 'sitecore\Sitecore Content Transfer' role; CORS via policy "ContentTransferCorsPolicy".
Exposed operations:
/ — discover available sources.
— upload a gzip or raw stream (default) to blob storage.
/ — start consuming a file or blob source into a database.
/ — inspect overall and per‑transfer status.
— review recent consumed sources across databases.
/ — browse and inspect items in a consumed source.
— check a blob’s current state and related info.
— retry a failed source; — discard a source and its data.
Examples:
Check blob state: GET …/ItemsTransfer/sources/blobs/content_2025-08-28.raif
Consume uploaded blob: POST …/ItemsTransfer/transfers/databases/master/sources?blobName=content_2025-08-28.raif

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV3Controller.ListTransfers(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Returns the status of consumed and transferred sources across all databases, including their transfer state and blob state.
member.param: The number of items per page for pagination.
member.returns: TransferStatusResultV3 object containing a list of TransferStatusV3 for all consumed and transferred sources across databases, along with pagination information.
member.remarks: Returns a paged list of currently available active and completed transfers across all Sitecore databases. Each entry includes original file name, transfer date, and transfer state. Transferred sources are loaded into memory sources, which will disappear after application restart. Alternatively, it is possible to see the history of source events to get information about past transfers. And use Blob Details to get information about source and its last transfer state. Paging, use and to navigate.
member.example: GET /{transfer}/v3/ItemsTransfer/transfers?page=1&pageSize=50

member.returns: An IHttpActionResult containing the details of the transferred source or an error result if the transfer is not found or not supported.

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV3Controller.ConsumeFile(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Starts consuming a file source into a database by validating the file, locking it for uploading, and then processing it asynchronously.
member.remarks: Initiates the content transfer from a local Sitecore file system source into the target . Use and afterwards to track progress. Return HTTP 202 Accepted and provides 'Location' header to check specific source transfers.
member.param: The name of the file to consume.
member.returns: An HTTP action result indicating the status of the operation.
member.example: POST /{transfer}/v3/ItemsTransfer/transfers/databases/{databaseName}/sources?fileName={fileName}

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV3Controller.ConsumeBlob(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Starts consuming a blob source into a specified database by validating the blob, locking it for uploading, and then processing it asynchronously.
member.remarks: Initiates the content transfer from an Azure Blob storage source into the target . Use afterwards to track progress tracking. Return HTTP 202 Accepted and provides 'Location' header to check specific blob details.
member.param: The name of the blob to consume.
member.returns: An HTTP action result indicating the status of the operation.
member.example: POST /{transfer}/v3/ItemsTransfer/transfers/databases/{databaseName}/sources?blobName={blobName}

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV3Controller.DiscardSource(System.String)
member.summary: Discards a transferred source by deleting its associated file or blob and marking it as discarded.
member.remarks: Performs the permanent removal of artifacts tracking across Blob storage and caches representing the passed source. Once this successfully completes, memory and remote allocations associated won't be recoverable except upon full re-consume operations.
member.param: The name of the blob source.
member.returns: NoContent status if the source was successfully discarded, or an ErrorResultV3 if the source cannot be discarded due to its current state, if it is not found, or if an error occurs during the deletion process.
member.example: DELETE /{transfer}/v3/ItemsTransfer/sources/blobs/{blobName}

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV3Controller.GetBlobDetails(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves the state of a specific blob source, including its transfer state, any associated errors, and the name of the consumed source if applicable.
member.remarks: Returns HTTP 200 containing containing the state of the blob source. If the blob does not exist it yields an HTTP 404 response. Includes validation breakdown when its BlobState reflects failures.

member.example: GET /{transfer}/v3/ItemsTransfer/sources/blobs/{blobName}

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.Transfer.ItemsTransferV3Controller.UploadBlob(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Uploads a blob to the system for processing, with an option to decompress if the blob is compressed using GZip. The method validates the blob name, retrieves the blob stream, and then uploads it using the transfer file blob provider.
member.remarks: Note that the file data is pushed using stream content chunks. Set query parameter to true if stream applies gzip algorithms. Return HTTP 201 Created and provides 'Location' header to check specific blob details.
member.param: The name of the blob to upload.
A flag indicating whether to decompress as GZip blob.
member.returns: An HTTP action result indicating the success or failure of the upload operation.
member.example: POST /{transfer}/v3/ItemsTransfer/sources/blobs/{blobName}?gzip={true|false}

member.name: M:Sitecore.Web.WebUtil.ParseQueryString(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Parses a query string into a dictionary of key/value pairs.
member.param: \ The query string. May include a path or URL prefix followed by a question mark separator. Only the first '?' is treated as the query separator; subsequent '?' characters in parameter values are preserved.
If set to true, applies HttpUtility.UrlDecode to parameter values.
member.returns: A dictionary containing the query string parameters.

remarks.para: The parameter list must have the format: "key1=value1&key2=value2&...".

Question mark handling: Only the FIRST '?' in the input string is treated as the query string separator. All subsequent '?' characters are preserved as part of parameter values. This allows regex patterns and other values containing '?' to be parsed correctly.

Examples:
"path/to/resource?key=value" → Skips first '?', parses parameters
"?key=value" → Skips first '?', parses parameters
"key=value" → No '?' to skip, parses parameters directly
"path?Result=Error&Pattern=\*\?" → First '?' skipped, '?' in Pattern value is preserved
